sourceEvidence.claim: Yersinia enterocolitica entry (gram ⊝ pleomorphic rod/coccobacillus with bipolar staining; pet feces, contaminated milk, pork; acute bloody diarrhea, pseudoappendicitis with mesenteric adenitis and/or terminal ileitis; reactive arthritis in adults)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Yersinia enterocolitica

Gram ⊝ pleomorphic rod/coccobacillus with bipolar staining. Usually transmitted from pet feces
(eg, cats, dogs), contaminated milk, or pork. Can cause acute bloody diarrhea, pseudoappendicitis
(right lower abdominal pain due to mesenteric adenitis and/or terminal ileitis), reactive arthritis in
adults.

sourceEvidence.claim: Klebsiella entry (lobar pneumonia in heavy alcohol use or impaired host defenses; very mucoid colonies with inline photo marker A; dark red currant-jelly sputum; healthcare-associated UTIs; MDR)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Klebsiella

Gram ⊝ rod; intestinal microbiota that causes
lobar pneumonia; more common in patients
with heavy alcohol use or with impaired host
defenses. Very mucoid colonies A caused by
abundant polysaccharide capsules. Dark red
“currant jelly” sputum (blood/mucus).
Also cause of healthcare-associated UTIs.
Associated with evolution of multidrug
resistance (MDR).

sourceEvidence.claim: Campylobacter jejuni entry (comma or S shaped with polar flagella and inline photo marker A; oxidase ⊕; grows at 42°C with the printed hot-campfire gloss; major cause of bloody diarrhea; fecal-oral with the personto-person merged hyphen-drop; common antecedent to Guillain-Barré syndrome and reactive arthritis)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Gram ⊝, comma or S shaped (with polar flagella) A , oxidase ⊕, grows at 42°C (“Campylobacter
likes the hot campfire”).
Major cause of bloody diarrhea, especially in children. Fecal-oral transmission through personto-person contact or via ingestion of undercooked contaminated poultry or meat, unpasteurized
milk. Contact with infected animals (dogs, cats, pigs) is also a risk factor.
Common antecedent to Guillain-Barré syndrome and reactive arthritis.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Proteus mirabilis entry (gram ⊝, urease ⊕, facultative anaerobe; swarming motility; common cause of UTIs; urease hydrolyzes urea with the → arrows; struvite stones and staghorn calculi)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Gram ⊝, urease ⊕, facultative anaerobe, long flagellae with “swarming” motility.
Common cause of UTIs. Urease (virulence factor) hydrolyzes urea to carbon dioxide and ammonia
→  net increase in pH →  promotes formation of struvite stones. Significant blockage of renal
calyces results in branched stones called staghorn calculi.

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the comparison table and the organism entries; the USMLE question attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The invasion-vs-toxigenic reading of the E. coli strain set (EIEC borrows Shigella's invasion, ETEC borrows the enterotoxin-only watery mechanism, EPEC adheres without either, EHEC borrows the Shiga toxin and adds the kidney) with the HUS cascade wired to nephrology; the dose axis as the public-health column (low acid-stable ID50 = person-to-person spread); the antibiotic-effect axis read as therapy-as-epidemiology (prolongs for both Salmonellas, shortens for Shigella); the MacConkey/EMB plate rule as the lactose-fermenter boundary; and the roster's exposure-to-disease map (pseudoappendicitis, currant-jelly pneumonia, Guillain-Barré antecedent, staghorn calculi) — labeled as integrations.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the tables and entries without the axis synthesis or the cross-chapter wiring; these integrations are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + both mechanism captions + callout + patterns + traps + mnemonics + miniCase
